name: inkscape-millimetre-scorebug
story: A sports-club volunteer drew a floorball scorebug on a 16:9 page set up in millimetres (Inkscape's default document unit), so the whole graphic lives inside a 338.66666 x 190.5 user-unit coordinate space, and saved it as Inkscape SVG.
idioms: width="338.66666mm" height="190.5mm" with viewBox="0 0 338.66666 190.5" - the physical unit is on width/height only
millimetre-scale numbers everywhere: font-size:8.99583px, stroke-width:0.264583, ry="1.5875"
a layer transform="translate(-4.7625,-6.35)" so no drawn coordinate is its on-screen position
text-align:end;text-anchor:end carried in the style attribute, and repeated on the tspan
seven-significant-digit decimals (22.754167, 8.9958334) from Inkscape's unit conversion
<g inkscape:label="Tulostaulu" inkscape:groupmode="layer"> with inkscape:label on each <text>
no <metadata> block (this file was saved over an existing one)
whyThisMatters: Inkscape defaults new documents to millimetres, so this is what a student's first file looks like. The drawn size is 338.66mm x 190.5mm, which is 1280 x 720 CSS px at the 96dpi the SVG spec fixes - the size docs/SVG_AUTHORING.md 2 promises drives the graphic ("the artwork's own size drives the graphic; NoaCG never rescales your geometry behind your back"). Catches an importer that reads the viewBox user units as pixels and lands a full-page design as a 339 x 191 postage stamp.
